sentences.text: The fourth trochanter of Ixalerpeton formed a large crest, a feature unlike that of Dromomeron.
Unlike Lagerpeton, the last few dorsal vertebrae of Ixalerpeton lack forward-inclining neural spines associated with a hopping lifestyle.
Ixalerpeton is distinguished by having an antitrochanter on the ilium, a tall ischium shaft end, and no ambiens process on the pubis.
The medial condyle on the Ixalerpeton femur is relatively flat at the front but sharply angled at the back.
An extra bone called the postfrontal borders the eye socket in Ixalerpeton.
Ixalerpeton lacks the supratemporal fossa, an indentation found on the frontal bone of dinosauriforms.
The glenoid cavity on the Ixalerpeton scapula faces slightly sideways rather than backwards.
The Ixalerpeton specimen was found in the Carnian-aged Santa Maria Formation of Brazil.
The species name polesinensis refers to the town of São João do Polêsine, the location of the excavation site.
Ixalerpeton is a genus of lagerpetid avemetatarsalian containing the single species I. polesinensis.
Ixalerpeton belongs to the family Lagerpetidae.
Ixalerpeton lived during the Carnian stage, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
Ixalerpeton lived in the Late Triassic of Brazil alongside the sauropodomorph dinosaur Buriolestes.
